To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclear lamin protein LINC1 plays a key role for PAMP-triggered immune responses and for regulation of jasmonic acid (and thus also of salicylic acid) signaling in plants.
LINC1 plays a key role for the regulation of PAMP-triggered responses and JA signaling in Arabidopsis.

the nuclear lamin protein LINC1 plays a key role during pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) in Arabidopsis, by regulating the expression of genes involved in the biosynthesis and perception of the hormone jasmonic acid (JAs) and by regulating JA signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the nuclear envelope and the nuclear pore complexes by plant lamin-like proteins and their role in plant immune responses.
the function of the Arabidopsis lamin-LIKE NUCLEI1 (LINC) in plant immunity.
the role of LINC proteins for plant immunity and JA signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LINC1 plays a key role as a regulator of PTI and JA signaling in Arabidopsis.
the nuclear envelope protein LINC1 plays a key role for the nuclear import of JA-related proteins and thus is required for the regulation of the JA pathway in Arabidopsis.
LINC1 is involved in the regulation of PTI, JA and SA signaling, and in JA-mediated defense against B. cinerea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LINC1 is an integral nuclear envelope component, which is important for nuclear gene regulation in the context of PAMP-triggered immune and JA signaling.
LINC1 is required for the proper functioning of the nuclear envelope and for the nuclear localization of the JA signaling pathway.
the LINC1 lamin-like protein regulates PAMP-triggered signaling to the nuclear envelope and thereby controls PAMP-triggered gene expression.

LINC1 is an essential regulator of PTI and JA signaling.
